priority_mapping.0: P0 / Not parallel-safe — must run alone

assumptions: Vibe is Mistral's open-source CLI coding assistant. Binary: `vibe`. Install: `uv tool install mistral-vibe` or `pip install mistral-vibe`. API key: MISTRAL_API_KEY (stored in ~/.vibe/.env). Docs: docs/tools/mistral/vibe.md.

Vibe programmatic invocation: `vibe --prompt '<task>' --agent auto-approve --output text`. Session resume: `vibe --resume <session_id> --agent auto-approve`. Session discovery requires reading vibe session logs.

Vibe uses AGENTS.md as its project context file (identical to codex). Both tools may be enabled simultaneously; context.protect: true must be documented as the safe default to avoid overwrite conflicts.

The adapter follows the exact same pattern as claude/codex/gemini: Rust crate in adapters/vibe/, self-registers via inventory::submit!, builds with the same dependency set (inventory, macc-core, macc-adapter-shared, serde, serde_json, regex).
core/build.rs auto-discovers all *.sh files under adapters/*/. Creating adapters/vibe/vibe.performer.sh is sufficient — no build.rs changes needed.

The ui-denylist.txt currently lists: claude, gemini, codex, gpt-4, gpt-3.5, anthropic, google, openai. 'vibe' and 'mistral' must be added for consistency. The is_allowed_occurrence() exemptions in core/tests/tool_name_guardrail.rs already cover loader.rs (registry/tools.d/*.tool.yaml paths) and normalizers — no new exemptions required.

registry/src/lib.rs contains an assertion `assert_eq!(ids.len(), 4)` that must be updated to 5 after adding vibe. The adapters/Cargo.toml workspace and registry/Cargo.toml dependency list require explicit vibe additions.
All vibe-specific logic stays inside adapters/vibe/. core/, cli/, tui/ must remain tool-agnostic. The adapter registers itself; the engine discovers it via the registry.
The emit layer generates: AGENTS.md (primary vibe context file, same structure as codex's AGENTS.md) and .vibe/config.toml (non-secret model/agent settings). API keys are never generated into files.

Tasks L5B-MAP-001 and L5B-ERR-001 can run in parallel after L5B-CRATE-001. L5B-EMIT-001 and L5B-ADAPTER-001 serialize after L5B-MAP-001. L5B-PERF-001 and L5B-GUARD-001 are independent of all Rust adapter tasks.

tasks.title: Create vibe.tool.yaml ToolSpec in registry/tools.d/
tasks.description:
Problem/Goal: MACC discovers tools via ToolSpec YAML files embedded in the registry. Without a vibe.tool.yaml, the TUI does not show vibe as an available tool, macc plan/apply cannot generate vibe config files, and the coordinator cannot dispatch tasks to vibe.
Key actions: Create registry/tools.d/vibe.tool.yaml following the exact structure of claude.tool.yaml and gemini.tool.yaml. Set: id=vibe, display_name=Vibe, description='Project instructions for Mistral Vibe CLI.'. gitignore: ['.vibe/', 'AGENTS.md']. performer.runner=adapters/vibe/vibe.performer.sh, performer.command=vibe, performer.args=['--agent', 'auto-approve', '--output', 'text'], performer.prompt.mode=arg, performer.prompt.arg='--prompt'. Session config: enabled=true, scope=worktree, init_prompt='Hello', resume.command=vibe, resume.args=['--resume', '{session_id}', '--agent', 'auto-approve', '--output', 'text']. defaults.model: a sensible default Mistral model (e.g. 'mistral-medium-3'). install: confirm_message + uv tool install mistral-vibe command, post_install verifying vibe --version. update: uv tool install --upgrade mistral-vibe. version_check.current: vibe --version. Fields: model (enum of Mistral model names), agent (enum: default, plan, accept-edits, auto-approve), skills (action: open_skills). doctor: which-check for vibe binary with severity=error.
Out of scope: Rust adapter implementation. Any changes to existing ToolSpecs. Session ID extraction strategy (will be refined when performer script is written).
Success criteria: registry/tools.d/vibe.tool.yaml is valid YAML that passes macc_core::tool::ToolSpec::from_yaml(). Its structure mirrors claude.tool.yaml / gemini.tool.yaml. 'id' field is exactly 'vibe'. performer.command is exactly 'vibe'. All required sections (performer, install, update, version_check, fields, doctor) are present.
tasks.objective: Declare vibe as a known MACC tool so it is discoverable by the ToolSpecLoader and usable in plan/apply/coordinator cycles.
tasks.result: registry/tools.d/vibe.tool.yaml exists and parses as a valid ToolSpec. The file mirrors the structure of existing ToolSpecs.
steps: Copy registry/tools.d/codex.tool.yaml as a starting template (codex also uses AGENTS.md and a similar programmatic invocation).
Update id, display_name, description, gitignore entries for vibe.
Set performer.command=vibe, performer.args for programmatic/auto-approve mode.
Configure session.resume with vibe --resume {session_id}.
Fill install section with uv tool install mistral-vibe and a post_install check.
Add version_check, update, and doctor sections following gemini/claude patterns.
Populate fields: model (Mistral model enum), agent (vibe agent enum), skills.
Validate YAML syntax (python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('registry/tools.d/vibe.tool.yaml'))" or equivalent).
tasks.notes: AGENTS.md is listed in gitignore because vibe writes its context into that file, which is the same file codex uses. When both tools are enabled, users should set tools.config.vibe.context.protect=true in macc.yaml to prevent MACC from overwriting an existing AGENTS.md that was generated by codex. Add a comment in the YAML noting this. The vibe default agent in programmatic mode should be 'auto-approve' — the performer_lib.sh reads args from tool.json so the ToolSpec is the canonical source.

tasks.title: Implement VibeConfig in adapters/vibe/src/map.rs
tasks.description:
Problem/Goal: The emit and adapter layers need a strongly-typed config struct that maps the MACC canonical config (ResolvedConfig) to vibe-specific settings. Without this, adapter.rs and the emit functions have no clean source of truth.
Key actions: Implement VibeConfig struct in adapters/vibe/src/map.rs. Fields: language: String, model: String (default: 'mistral-medium-3' or equivalent Mistral coding model — match what is listed in the ToolSpec), agent: String (default: 'auto-approve'), skills: Vec<String>, tool_config: serde_json::Value, has_mcp: bool. Implement VibeConfig::from_resolved(resolved: &ResolvedConfig) -> Self. Logic: read tool_config from resolved.tools.config.get('vibe') or resolved.tools.specific.get('vibe'), deserialize a VibeConfigSource (serde Deserialize) from it, merge global resolved.selections.skills with tool-specific skills using BTreeSet for deduplication and stable ordering. Mirror the pattern in adapters/claude/src/map.rs and adapters/codex/src/map.rs exactly.
Out of scope: Emit functions. Adapter plan() logic. Any vibe-specific model validation.
Success criteria: VibeConfig::from_resolved() compiles without warnings. Unit tests: default model when no config provided, skills merged from global + tool-specific selections, agent defaults to 'auto-approve' when not set in config. Mirrors codex/claude map.rs test patterns.
tasks.objective: Provide a clean, testable config mapping layer that decouples vibe-specific settings from the canonical MACC config model.
tasks.result: adapters/vibe/src/map.rs with VibeConfig, VibeConfigSource, and from_resolved() implementation. Unit tests pass. Replaces the stub from L5B-CRATE-001.
steps: Define VibeConfigSource with #[derive(Deserialize, Default)] and optional fields: model, language, agent, skills (Vec<String>).
Define VibeConfig with concrete (non-optional) fields and their resolved defaults.
Implement from_resolved(): extract tool_config, deserialize VibeConfigSource, merge global + tool-specific skills with BTreeSet, set defaults for missing fields.
Write unit tests: test_default_model_when_no_config(), test_skills_merged(), test_agent_default_is_auto_approve().
Run cargo test -p macc-adapter-vibe -- map.
tasks.notes: The model field default should match the ToolSpec's defaults.model field exactly so the two sources of truth are consistent. If the model name changes in the ToolSpec, this file must change too — note this coupling in a comment. Use BTreeSet for skill deduplication to ensure deterministic ordering (same approach as ClaudeConfig). The 'agent' field controls which vibe agent profile is used for non-interactive runs — 'auto-approve' is the correct value for performer execution.

tasks.title: Implement emit layer: AGENTS.md and .vibe/config.toml renderers
tasks.description:
Problem/Goal: The adapter's plan() function needs render functions to produce vibe's two config files: AGENTS.md (project context, loaded by vibe on startup) and .vibe/config.toml (non-secret model and agent settings). These renderers must be pure functions over VibeConfig so they are testable in isolation.
Key actions: Create adapters/vibe/src/emit/mod.rs re-exporting agents_md and config_toml submodules. Create adapters/vibe/src/emit/agents_md.rs with pub fn render_agents_md(config: &VibeConfig) -> String. The AGENTS.md content should include: a header comment identifying it as MACC-generated, standards summary from config.standards_inline, required workflows section (run tests before committing, use English), and a Vibe-specific skills section listing active skills. Mirror adapters/codex/src/emit/agents_md.rs structure. Create adapters/vibe/src/emit/config_toml.rs with pub fn render_config_toml(config: &VibeConfig) -> String. The .vibe/config.toml content should include: default_agent (from config.agent — 'auto-approve' for programmatic use), active_model (from config.model). Do NOT include API keys, passwords, or secrets. Use toml::to_string or manual string building — if toml crate is not yet in dependencies, add it to adapters/vibe/Cargo.toml. Call macc_adapter_shared::render::format::ensure_trailing_newline on all outputs.
Out of scope: AGENTS.md content specific to other tools. MCP server configuration rendering (can be a follow-up if needed — vibe supports MCP but it is optional). User-level ~/.vibe/ config (MACC only generates project-level files).
Success criteria: render_agents_md() returns a string containing the standards section and required workflows. render_config_toml() returns a valid TOML string with default_agent and active_model keys. Neither function contains secrets or API key strings. Unit tests verify output structure for both renderers.
tasks.objective: Produce the two config files that vibe reads on startup: AGENTS.md (task context) and .vibe/config.toml (non-secret settings).
tasks.result: adapters/vibe/src/emit/mod.rs, adapters/vibe/src/emit/agents_md.rs, adapters/vibe/src/emit/config_toml.rs. All render functions compile and have unit tests. Replaces the stub emit/mod.rs from L5B-CRATE-001.

Create emit/config_toml.rs with render_config_toml(config: &VibeConfig) -> String emitting [default_agent] and [active_model] TOML keys.

The file must not contain MISTRAL_API_KEY — vibe reads that from ~/.vibe/.env automatically. Setting `active_model` in .vibe/config.toml configures the model for the vibe session. If the toml crate adds complexity, use format! string building for the small config.toml output instead.

tasks.title: Implement VibeAdapter in adapters/vibe/src/adapter.rs
tasks.description:
Problem/Goal: VibeAdapter is the core integration point. Its plan() method produces the ActionPlan that MACC's engine translates into file writes during macc apply. Without a complete adapter.rs, the tool cannot generate any project config files.
Key actions: Implement VibeAdapter in adapters/vibe/src/adapter.rs, replacing the stub from L5B-CRATE-001. Implement ToolAdapter trait: id() returns 'vibe'. plan(ctx: &PlanningContext) -> Result<ActionPlan>: create VibeConfig::from_resolved(ctx.resolved), build an ActionPlan, call plan_builders::write_text to emit AGENTS.md (using emit::agents_md::render_agents_md), call plan_builders::write_text to emit .vibe/config.toml (using emit::config_toml::render_config_toml). Handle remote content: iterate ctx.materialized_units → for skills call plan_builders::plan_skill_install('vibe', ...), for MCP entries call plan_builders::plan_mcp_install. The pattern is identical to adapters/claude/src/adapter.rs fn install_remote_content(). For .mcp.json rendering (MCP server wiring): if any MCP servers are present, render and write .mcp.json using macc_core::mcp_json::render_mcp_json — vibe supports MCP via [[mcp_servers]] in config.toml but .mcp.json is the MACC-canonical approach; note in a comment that a future task can add mcp_servers into .vibe/config.toml directly.
Out of scope: Session management. Error normalization. Doctor checks. Changing macc_core plan_builders API.
Success criteria: VibeAdapter implements ToolAdapter. plan() returns a non-empty ActionPlan containing at least two write actions (AGENTS.md and .vibe/config.toml). cargo test -p macc-adapter-vibe passes. No new warnings.

tasks.title: Implement VibeErrorNormalizer in adapters/vibe/src/error_normalizer.rs
tasks.description:
Problem/Goal: The coordinator's rate-limit handling, retry logic, and error reporting depend on each adapter providing a tool-specific ErrorNormalizer that maps raw CLI output (stderr/stdout) to canonical CanonicalClass values. Without VibeErrorNormalizer, vibe failures appear as UnknownError with no retry strategy.
Key actions: Replace the stub VibeErrorNormalizer in adapters/vibe/src/error_normalizer.rs with a full implementation following adapters/claude/src/error_normalizer.rs exactly. Define a Pattern list (Regex + CanonicalClass pairs) for Mistral-specific error messages. Priority order (same as claude): (1) QuotaExhausted — 'usage limit', 'quota exceeded', 'resets N(am|pm)' for Mistral usage cap messages; (2) Auth — 'unauthorized', 'invalid api key', 'authentication failed', MISTRAL_API_KEY error messages; (3) PolicyViolation — Mistral content policy rejection patterns; (4) Billing — 'payment required', 'billing error'; (5) Overloaded — '529' or 'server overloaded' (Mistral uses similar codes); (6) RateLimit — '429', 'too many requests', 'rate limit'; (7) Network — ECONNREFUSED/ETIMEDOUT/DNS patterns (same as claude); (8) Timeout — timeout/timed out; (9) Internal — '500 internal server error'. Implement ErrorNormalizer::normalize(exit_code, stderr, stdout) -> Option<ToolError>. Extract request_id from Mistral-specific request ID patterns if available. Extract retry-after from '429' responses if a retry-after header value appears in stderr.
Out of scope: Changing CanonicalClass definitions or error codes. Adding new canonical classes. Modifying shared normalizer helpers.
Success criteria: VibeErrorNormalizer implements ErrorNormalizer. normalize() returns QuotaExhausted for 'usage limit exceeded', RateLimit for '429 Too Many Requests', Auth for 'invalid api key', None for exit 0 with clean output. Unit tests cover each CanonicalClass case. cargo test -p macc-adapter-vibe passes.
tasks.objective: Enable the coordinator to classify, retry, and report vibe errors correctly using the same canonical error model as all other tools.
tasks.result: adapters/vibe/src/error_normalizer.rs with VibeErrorNormalizer and comprehensive unit tests for each error class. Replaces stub from L5B-CRATE-001.
steps: Import OnceLock, Regex, and error_normalizer utilities from macc_adapter_shared.
Define Mistral-specific Pattern list (Regex + CanonicalClass) in priority order, following claude's pattern list structure.
Implement normalize(): combine stderr+stdout, run patterns, fall back to Unknown on non-zero exit, return None on exit 0 with no match.
Extract retry_after_seconds from '429' retry-after text if present.
Set provider field to 'vibe' in the returned ToolError.
Write unit tests covering each canonical class plus exit-0-clean, unknown-non-zero-exit, and raw-message-truncation cases.
Run cargo test -p macc-adapter-vibe -- error_normalizer.
tasks.notes: Mistral API error messages may differ slightly from Anthropic's — check the Mistral API docs if specific error JSON format is known. In absence of Mistral-specific documentation, use the same regex patterns as claude for network/timeout/internal errors (these are OS-level and tool-agnostic) and customize only the quota/auth/billing patterns. Use chrono for retry-after timestamp parsing if quota messages include a reset time in Mistral format — add chrono to Cargo.toml if needed. The provider field must be exactly 'vibe' (matching the ToolSpec id field).

tasks.title: Create adapters/vibe/vibe.performer.sh performer script
tasks.description:
Problem/Goal: The coordinator dispatches tasks to a tool by invoking its performer script. Without adapters/vibe/vibe.performer.sh, the coordinator cannot run vibe tasks — even if the Rust adapter and ToolSpec are complete.
Key actions: Create adapters/vibe/vibe.performer.sh following the exact pattern of adapters/codex/codex.performer.sh and adapters/claude/claude.performer.sh. The file must: (1) set TOOL_ID='vibe' and TOOL_LOG_PREFIX='vibe'; (2) resolve script_dir using $BASH_SOURCE; (3) source $script_dir/../shared/performer_lib.sh. This is the complete and correct content — the shared performer_lib.sh handles all argument parsing, session management, and tool invocation by reading the tool.json that comes from the ToolSpec (L5B-SPEC-001). Mark the file executable (chmod 755). Note: core/build.rs auto-discovers all *.sh files in adapters/*/. Creating this file is sufficient — it will be embedded automatically into the MACC binary and deployed to .macc/automation/embedded/adapters/vibe/ during macc apply.
Out of scope: Any performer logic beyond sourcing the shared library. Changes to shared/performer_lib.sh.
Success criteria: adapters/vibe/vibe.performer.sh exists, is executable (mode 755), contains exactly TOOL_ID='vibe', TOOL_LOG_PREFIX='vibe', and the source line for performer_lib.sh. Running shellcheck adapters/vibe/vibe.performer.sh produces no errors. Running bash -n adapters/vibe/vibe.performer.sh succeeds (syntax check).
tasks.objective: Provide the minimal performer script that lets the coordinator invoke vibe for task execution.
tasks.result: adapters/vibe/vibe.performer.sh exists, is executable, and is syntactically valid. The script is automatically embedded by core/build.rs and deployed by macc apply.

Replace TOOL_ID='codex' with TOOL_ID='vibe' and TOOL_LOG_PREFIX='codex' with TOOL_LOG_PREFIX='vibe'.
Verify the source path is correct relative to the new script location (should be $script_dir/../shared/performer_lib.sh — same relative path).
chmod 755 adapters/vibe/vibe.performer.sh.

Optionally run shellcheck adapters/vibe/vibe.performer.sh.

The TOOL_ID and TOOL_LOG_PREFIX values must match the ToolSpec id field ('vibe') exactly — mismatches cause performer log routing errors. tasks.title: Wire VibeAdapter into registry/src/lib.rs and update registry tests
tasks.description:
Problem/Goal: The Rust linker includes an adapter only if it is referenced from the linked binary. registry/src/lib.rs uses a forced-reference pattern (let _ = (...AdapterType...)) to ensure inventory::submit! fires for each adapter. Without adding VibeAdapter here, the adapter is silently excluded even though its crate is a dependency.
